name: Concurrent MutableString append agrees across backends

input.fixture_ref: fixture: {source: "m = m\"x\"; gate = Barrier.new(3); results = Concurrent.collect([ { gate.wait(); m.append(\"é\") }, { gate.wait(); m.append(\"😀\") } ]); gate.wait(); Concurrent.join_all(); snapshot = m.to_string(); [results, snapshot, snapshot.to_bytes()]"}

applicability.reason: Genuinely blocked on a second backend, verified rather than assumed. A DIFFERENTIAL row asserts that the interpreter and the JIT agree, which is only meaningful when both exist: with one backend any such comparison is self-agreement and proves nothing. The workspace has seven crates - iris-abi, iris-conformance, iris-eval, iris-lexer, iris-parser, iris-runtime, iris-syntax - and no JIT or AOT crate, feature or Cargo entry anywhere. This is not a missing surface that could be added alongside the others; it waits on the VM the owner has already scheduled separately. This row compounds that with the concurrency blocker COLLECTIONS-V908 records: runtime values are `Rc<RefCell<..>>` and therefore not `Send`, so no Iris value can cross a thread boundary today either. Both must be resolved before the row is observable.

expect.status: Each backend observes either one ConcurrentMutationError with snapshot exactly "xé" or "x😀", or two successes with snapshot exactly "xé😀" or "x😀é"; Bytes are respectively 78c3a9, 78f09f9880, 78c3a9f09f9880, or 78f09f9880c3a9, never invalid or partial UTF-8.
